subject: math
cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
intro: Eight multiple-choice questions on using units to set up and check multi-step problems: building and orienting conversion factors, chaining factors, converting compound rates, keeping units consistent in formulas, and reading or choosing a graph scale and origin.

items.prompt:
Convert $7$ feet to inches using $1\text{ ft}=12\text{ in}$.
A) $\frac{7}{12}\text{ in}$
B) $19\text{ in}$
C) $84\text{ in}$
D) $0.58\text{ in}$

steps: Orient the conversion factor so feet cancels: $7\text{ ft}\times\frac{12\text{ in}}{1\text{ ft}}$.
The ft units cancel, leaving inches: $7\times 12=84\text{ in}$. Key is C.
A inverts the factor, multiplying by $\frac{1}{12}$ instead of $12$, giving $\frac{7}{12}$ in.
B adds $7+12$ instead of multiplying.
D divides $7\div 12$, the same inversion error as A written as a decimal.

items.prompt:
Convert $48$ inches to feet using $1\text{ ft}=12\text{ in}$.
A) $4\text{ ft}$
B) $576\text{ ft}$
C) $36\text{ ft}$
D) $60\text{ ft}$

steps: To cancel inches, the conversion factor must have inches in the denominator: $48\text{ in}\times\frac{1\text{ ft}}{12\text{ in}}$.
This gives $48\div 12=4\text{ ft}$. Key is A.
B multiplies by $12$ instead of dividing, the wrong-operation error.
C subtracts $48-12$ instead of dividing.
D adds $48+12$ instead of dividing.

items.prompt:
A bar graph's vertical axis starts at $0$ and each gridline represents $250$ units. A bar reaches exactly the $3$rd gridline above zero. What value does the bar show?
A) $3$
B) $253$
C) $750$
D) $250$

steps: Each gridline is worth $250$, so the value at the $n$th gridline is $250n$.
At the $3$rd gridline: $250\times 3=750$. Key is C.
A reads the gridline number $3$ as the value, ignoring the stated interval.
B adds $3+250$ instead of multiplying.
D reads only one gridline interval, not three.

items.prompt:
Convert $2$ miles to inches using $1\text{ mi}=5280\text{ ft}$ and $1\text{ ft}=12\text{ in}$.
A) $10560\text{ in}$
B) $24000\text{ in}$
C) $126720\text{ in}$
D) $880\text{ in}$

steps: Chain both factors so mi and ft cancel: $2\text{ mi}\times\frac{5280\text{ ft}}{1\text{ mi}}\times\frac{12\text{ in}}{1\text{ ft}}$.
Compute: $2\times 5280=10560\text{ ft}$, then $10560\times 12=126720\text{ in}$. Key is C.
A stops after the first factor and reports feet ($10560$) as if it were inches, leaving out the ft-to-in step.
B uses the wrong conversion value $1\text{ mi}=1000\text{ ft}$, giving $2\times 1000\times 12=24000$, a wrong-number error.
D divides by $12$ instead of multiplying at the last step ($10560\div 12=880$), an inverted final factor.

items.prompt:
Using distance $=$ rate $\times$ time, a runner moves at $8\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$ for $5$ minutes. How far does the runner travel?
A) $40\text{ ft}$
B) $2400\text{ ft}$
C) $1.6\text{ ft}$
D) $480\text{ ft}$

steps: The rate is in feet per second, so the time must be in seconds: $5\text{ min}\times\frac{60\text{ s}}{1\text{ min}}=300\text{ s}$.
Then $d=8\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}\times 300\text{ s}=2400\text{ ft}$. Key is B.
A substitutes $5$ min directly without converting: $8\times 5=40$, ignoring that units must match.
C divides instead of multiplying, $8\div 5$.
D uses $60$ s as the time instead of $300$ s, converting only $1$ minute.

items.prompt:
Daily high temperatures for a week range from $52^{\circ}\text{F}$ to $89^{\circ}\text{F}$. Which choice of vertical-axis scale and origin best displays this data?
A) Origin $0^{\circ}$, scale $10^{\circ}$ per gridline
B) Origin $50^{\circ}$, scale $5^{\circ}$ per gridline
C) Origin $0^{\circ}$, scale $1^{\circ}$ per gridline
D) Origin $90^{\circ}$, scale $5^{\circ}$ per gridline

steps: The data clusters between $52^{\circ}$ and $89^{\circ}$, so a nonzero origin near $50^{\circ}$ keeps the bars or points spread across the axis.
A scale of $5^{\circ}$ per gridline covers the $50^{\circ}$ to $90^{\circ}$ range in about $8$ gridlines, a readable spacing. Key is B.
A starts at $0$, wasting most of the axis below $52^{\circ}$ and flattening the differences.
C starts at $0$ and would need about $90$ gridlines at $1^{\circ}$ each, far too many.
D starts at $90^{\circ}$, above all the data, so every value would fall below the origin.

items.prompt:
A car travels at $90\ \frac{\text{mi}}{\text{hr}}$. Convert this speed to $\frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$ using $1\text{ mi}=5280\text{ ft}$ and $1\text{ hr}=3600\text{ s}$.
A) $132\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$
B) $475200\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$
C) $7920\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$
D) $0.025\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$

steps: Convert both the numerator and the denominator: $90\ \frac{\text{mi}}{\text{hr}}\times\frac{5280\text{ ft}}{1\text{ mi}}\times\frac{1\text{ hr}}{3600\text{ s}}$.
The mi and hr units cancel: $\frac{90\times 5280}{3600}=\frac{475200}{3600}=132\ \frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$. Key is A.
B converts only the numerator ($90\times 5280=475200$) and reports $\frac{\text{ft}}{\text{hr}}$ as if it were $\frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$, never dividing by $3600$.
C divides $475200$ by $60$ instead of $3600$, using the wrong value $1\text{ hr}=60\text{ s}$, giving $7920$.
D converts only the denominator, computing $90\div 3600=0.025$ and leaving the miles unconverted, so the units are still $\frac{\text{mi}}{\text{s}}$ rather than $\frac{\text{ft}}{\text{s}}$.

items.prompt:
In the work formula $W=Fd$, force $F$ is measured in newtons ($\text{N}$) and distance $d$ in meters ($\text{m}$). What are the units of $W$?
A) $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$
B) $\frac{\text{N}}{\text{m}}$
C) $\text{N}$
D) $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{N}}$

steps: Units multiply just as the quantities do: $W=F\times d$ gives units $\text{N}\times\text{m}=\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ (a joule).
Key is A.
B divides the units, as if $W=\frac{F}{d}$, but the formula multiplies.
C drops the distance unit entirely, treating $d$ as if it had no units.
D inverts the product into $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{N}}$, again treating multiplication as division.
